job_title: Member of Technical Staff (Software Engineer, Monetization)
section_intro:
Millions of people now use Perplexity to transform knowledge into action, and every action an agent takes is metered, budgeted, and settled through the billing platform this role owns.
As a monetization engineer at Perplexity, you'll own the abstractions that let product teams ship new SKUs, run pricing experiments, and convert users into paying customers, without needing to understand billing internals.
The usage-based billing system this team owns is foundational to Perplexity Computer and our agentic products: metering every agent action in real time, enforcing credit budgets, and settling costs across entirely new interaction models.
You'll work across subscriptions, usage-based billing, and enterprise contracts to ensure every revenue path is reliable, observable, and easy to extend.
Tech Stack: Python | Go | Stripe | PostgreSQL | AWS | Docker
- Craftsmanship.
- Ownership.
- Entrepreneurship.
- Scholarship.
- Partnership.
section_responsibilities:
- Design, build, and own the billing platform and monetization systems that power Computer and every paid experience across Perplexity.
- Lead features end-to-end, from problem definition through technical design, implementation, and launch, including the billing API abstractions that let product teams ship new SKUs, pricing models, and monetization experiments with minimal friction.
- Build and operate the subscription, invoicing, and usage-based billing systems that serve millions of users across consumer and enterprise plans.
- Hill-climb on reliability: tiered SLOs organized by customer impact, proactive monitoring, and alerting to catch revenue-affecting issues before customers do.
- Partner closely with Finance, Data Science, Growth, Security, Support, and go-to-market teams to keep billing data accurate, auditable, and compliant, and to expand payment method coverage and optimize authorization rates globally.
- Build internal tooling that empowers Support and Finance to diagnose and resolve billing issues quickly.
section_requirements:
- 4+ years of professional software engineering experience.
- Direct experience building or scaling billing, payments, subscription, or monetization systems.
- Deep familiarity with payment processors (Stripe, Square, etc.), including subscriptions, invoicing, disputes, refunds, and webhooks.
- Demonstrated experience and appetite for building in-house billing solutions that rival leading best-in-class buy options.
- Strong backend engineering skills in Python with the ability to reason about complex distributed systems.
- Experience with relational databases (PostgreSQL) and making data-informed decisions to prioritize work.
- Strong product judgment, you translate user and stakeholder problems into simple, effective technical solutions.
- Self-motivated with strong ownership instincts, you ship major features ahead of schedule and drive improvements without asking for permission.
- Track record of cross-functional collaboration with Finance, Support, or Growth stakeholders.
section_preferred:
- 2+ years of hands-on experience with the Stripe APIs and SDKs.
- Experience with usage-based or metered billing models, especially metering agent actions, tokens, or other non-traditional units.
- Experience with Apple and Google Play in-app purchase billing.
- Familiarity with growth experimentation and PLG/self-serve SaaS monetization.
- Experience building platform constructs that support pricing experiments and A/B testing.
- Full-stack experience (our frontend is Next.js/React/TypeScript).
- Experience in a regulatory or compliance-heavy billing environment.

section_intro:
We're looking for a Growth Brand Designer to sit at the intersection of brand craft and growth performance.
You'll be the designer who makes Perplexity's highest-volume, highest-leverage marketing surfaces - paid ads, social, lifecycle email, and campaign assets - look unmistakably Perplexity while actually moving the numbers.

Strategic concepting is a big part of the job: you'll sit with the Growth team as an ideator - generating campaign concepts, testing hypotheses, and shaping the creative strategy behind the work - not just executing briefs handed to you.
The ideas you bring to the table matter as much as the assets you ship.
You'll produce a steady stream of ad and campaign creative across formats and channels, then work with Growth to read the results and iterate.
You care about conversion and craft in equal measure: you'd never ship an off-brand asset to win a test, and you'd never hide behind polish when the data says a concept isn't working.

- Design for volume and velocity: build variant sets, test hypotheses, and iterate on winners with the Growth team using real performance data

- Partner with Brand to keep visual consistency across every growth touchpoint as our brand system evolves

Perplexity is looking for a Content Designer to shape the words across our products.
You'll design the language people see and hear across our family of Perplexity apps, from the first screen of onboarding to the way an agent explains what it's doing.
Fundamentally, we are all writers.
Our product is primarily spoken language and written product; but as we scale, we want someone who will continue to work on clarity, usefulness, and keep it unmistakably Perplexity.
You're a designer first?
You're an engineer first?
You're a writer first?
Your shape is not conventional, and you wear many hats.
You are fluent in AI tooling.
You have strong UX fundamentals and good product instincts.
You use language to solve product problems: flows, naming, information architecture, error states, permissions, and moments where people need to trust what the product is telling them.
You command words.
You command agents, and make decisions about words.
You can write one perfect line, and you can build the system that keeps thousands of lines consistent.
You'll sit on the Design Systems team and work closely with product designers, engineers, PMs, research, brand, and marketing.
(Again) You're fluent in AI-powered tools and use it every day.
You understand how models behave, how prompts and system instructions shape what people see, and how to define and judge quality when the output isn't fully deterministic.
section_responsibilities:
- Design and write in-product language across web, mobile, desktop, and voice, including UI copy, flows, onboarding, notifications, empty states, errors, and in-product education
- Partner with product designers from the start of a project, shaping flows, structure, and information architecture as well as the words in them
- Name features and products, and own terminology, navigation labels, and taxonomies so the product stays easy to understand as it grows
- Make complex AI and agent behavior understandable, including what the product is doing, why, what it can't do, and when it needs a person's input
- Shape how AI-generated content reads by writing and refining prompts and system instructions, and help define voice and response style for our models in product
- Define content quality standards and help build evaluation criteria, datasets, and reviewer guidance for AI-generated content
- Build and maintain voice and tone guidelines, content patterns, and content guidance in our design system so every team can write well
- Use research, data, and experiments to test language and improve comprehension, activation, and task completion
- Partner with brand and marketing so product language and our external voice feel like one company
- Work with internationalization partners so the product reads well in every language we support
- Review copy in code and ship small language changes directly when it's the fastest path
WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR
- 5+ years of experience in content design, UX writing, or product design, shipping software at scale
- An excellent portfolio that shows how your language shaped product decisions, with clear before and after examples and your role in each
- Strong UX fundamentals, including interaction design, information architecture, usability, and accessibility
- Good product sensibility and judgment about what to build, what to cut, and what matters most to people
- Exceptional writing and editing skills, with range from precise interface copy to clear explanations and confident naming
- Strong AI fluency, including hands-on experience writing prompts, working with LLMs, and judging the quality of AI-generated content
- Systems thinking, with experience building content frameworks, style guides, or terminology that scale across teams
- Clear communication, with the ability to explain content decisions and tradeoffs to designers, engineers, and leaders
- You care about shipping great software more than anything else
section_preferred:
- Experience designing content for AI products, assistants, agents, or conversational interfaces
- Experience with prompt engineering, model evals, or working with research teams on model behavior
- Experience across consumer and enterprise products, including admin, permissions, privacy, and billing flows
- Comfort working in code, such as editing strings, reviewing PRs, or prototyping with AI tools
- Experience with localization and writing for global audiences
NOTES FOR CANDIDATES
We want to see portfolio work where your words changed the product.
Show us the problem, the options you explored, the language you shipped, and what happened after.
We value end-to-end ownership, range, and impact, and we'd love to see examples of AI-related work, such as prompts, evaluations, or content you designed for model output.

The Cloud Infrastructure team owns the foundational cloud primitives and deployment models that power Perplexity's products, from multi-tenant public cloud to single-tenant and on-premises solutions for enterprise customers.
As Perplexity grows its Computer and Enterprise products, this team builds and operates the security, isolation, and compliance layers that customers depend on.

section_intro:
Perplexity serves hundreds of millions of queries a month.
Every answer, every Perplexity Computer task, and every enterprise deployment runs on production infrastructure owned by the Cloud Infrastructure team: a fleet of Kubernetes clusters across a multi-account AWS estate, private networks that reach hyperscalers and the neoclouds serving our models, and the storage underneath our user data and agentic workloads.
We're looking for SREs who treat reliability as a software problem.
You'll own compute, networking, and storage at scale and keep production stable while everything built on top of it is changing fast.
section_responsibilities:
- Own production at scale.
Run the compute, networking, and storage foundation behind Perplexity's consumer, Computer, API, and enterprise products, and own its availability, latency, and cost.
- Run our Kubernetes fleet.
Operate and upgrade the EKS clusters that host web services, search, datastores, and secure sandboxes.
Tune scheduling, autoscaling, node lifecycle, DNS, and service networking so clusters stay healthy under bursty, fast-growing load.
- Engineer the network.
Design and operate VPC architectures, Transit Gateway and PrivateLink connectivity, load balancing, DNS, and egress across accounts, regions, and cloud providers.
- Keep data durable and fast.
Own the storage layer (EBS, S3, DynamoDB, and the managed databases and caches our services depend on), including performance, durability, backups, and restores that have actually been tested.
- Manage everything as code.
Run infrastructure through Terraform and CI/CD.
Build reusable modules and guardrails, and make every change reviewable, repeatable, and safe to roll back.
- Prepare for failures.
Define SLOs, build alerts that someone can act on, design for zone and regional failure, and run game days and disaster-recovery exercises that prove recovery works.
- Lead incident response.
Be on the critical path when things break.
Drive incidents to resolution, write blameless postmortems, and land the fixes so the same failure never pages anyone twice.
- Scale ahead of demand.
Own capacity planning, quotas, reservations, and cost efficiency so product launches and traffic spikes never wait on infrastructure.

Build tooling, increasingly agent-driven, that turns provisioning, upgrades, and remediation into self-serve, hands-off workflows for every engineering team.

section_intro:
Perplexity is AI for people who expect more.
This role brings that standard to how we understand our users, shape our product, and decide what to build next.
We're looking for a data scientist who can turn product questions into clear decisions.
You'll work across product, engineering, growth, design, and user research to understand user behavior, define metrics, design experiments, and identify the highest-leverage opportunities for the company.
The data team is AI-native by default.
We use AI to accelerate analysis, write and review code, explore hypotheses, document data, generate first drafts, and automate recurring workflows.
But the core of the role is still judgment: asking the right question, choosing the right metric, designing the right test, and knowing when the answer is strong enough to act on.
section_responsibilities:
- Develop product insights - analyze user behavior to inform product roadmap, accelerate adoption, and identify opportunities to improve the user experience.
- Design and analyze experiments - form hypotheses, define success metrics, run A/B tests, interpret results, and turn findings into product recommendations.
- Define the metrics that matter - build the metrics, guardrails, dashboards, and reporting workflows that help teams understand product and company health.
- Partner across functions - work closely with engineering, product, growth, design, and user research to answer ambiguous questions and drive decisions.
- Build reusable data assets - create tables, models, and documentation that make analysis faster, more consistent, and easier for humans and AI systems to use.
- Use AI to scale data science - automate recurring analysis, build AI-assisted workflows, improve documentation, and turn one-off investigations into repeatable systems.
- Tell the story clearly - communicate findings, assumptions, uncertainty, and recommendations in a way that helps teams make decisions.
WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR
- 6+ years of experience as a data scientist or closely related role.
- Strong product sense - you understand user behavior, product tradeoffs, and how to connect analysis to decisions.
- SQL expertise - you can navigate a complex data warehouse on your own, reason about grain and joins, and debug data issues when something looks wrong.
- Experimentation depth - you have significant experience designing, running, and analyzing A/B tests.
- AI-native working style - you use LLMs and AI tools to move faster without outsourcing analytical judgment.
- Metrics and dashboard experience - you've built useful reporting in tools such as Omni, Mode, Hex, Looker, or similar, and know how to turn metrics into better product decisions.
- Comfort with ambiguity - you can take an open-ended question, structure it, execute the analysis, and make a clear recommendation.
- End-to-end ownership - you take responsibility for the work from problem definition to stakeholder adoption.
BONUS
- Experience with dbt, data modeling, or analytics engineering.
- Python experience for analysis, automation, or internal tools.
- Experience with Snowflake, especially performance and cost-aware querying.
- Experience combining qualitative user research with quantitative product analysis.
- Experience as one of the first data scientists at an early or growth-stage company.
- ML experience or experience working across multiple product surfaces.
WHY THIS ROLE
- Define data science at Perplexity - you'll help set the bar for how an AI-native data science team operates.
- Work on questions with no playbook - AI-native products are too new for established benchmarks.

- Use AI where it actually matters - you'll use frontier tools to make analysis faster, more repeatable, and more useful.
- Direct impact - small team, high ownership, and work that shapes product and company direction.

section_about:
The Enterprise Agent Evals & Efficiency team makes Perplexity's agents better at completing real work across enterprise connectors, tools, and data.

This team owns the improvement loop: define what successful work looks like, build evaluations that measure it, understand where agents fail, and ship changes that improve outcomes.
This is a hands-on engineering role with end-to-end ownership, from building realistic enterprise evaluation environments to shipping improvements across the agent harness, tools, and skills.
You'll create complex scenarios spanning connected systems, data, and permissions, use them to identify where agents struggle, and improve the tools agents call, the skills they follow, the context they receive, and the models they use.
Working with AI Research, Connectors, and Platform teams, you'll turn experimental results into measurable gains in task success, latency, and cost per successful task.
The goal is not just to measure agents, but to make more enterprise work reliable and practical to automate.

- Analyze agent trajectories and production failures, identify root causes, and ship improvements across the agent harness, tools, and skills that measurably improve task success and reliability.
- Develop reusable skills and improve tool descriptions, schemas, and result handling so agents can select the right tools, execute workflows correctly, and recover from errors with fewer unnecessary calls.
- Build and evaluate model-selection and routing strategies that match each task to the right model and effort level, balancing quality, latency, reliability, and cost.
- Improve agent efficiency through context management, skill loading, caching, and execution strategies that reduce wasted tokens and cost per successful task without compromising quality or safety.
- Build regression gates and launch-readiness signals for model, connector, tool, skill, and harness changes, and validate that evaluation gains translate into better production outcomes.

section_intro:
We're hiring a Legal Response Specialist on Perplexity's Support team to handle legal and other sensitive tickets.
You'll help Legal answer routine requests for information and support Governance, Risk & Compliance, or GRC, on privacy and security requests.
You'll review cases, write responses, and follow up until the work is done.
Support Engineering owns the routing and safeguards that keep these tickets from being missed, answered by AI, or automatically closed.
section_responsibilities:
- Monitor designated Support and Legal channels, assess urgency, and route requests for human review.
Promptly escalate government, court, law enforcement, and legal-threat requests according to approved procedures.
- Respond to routine requests using Legal-approved templates and guidance.
Escalate matters requiring legal interpretation or disclosure of user information.
- Answer routine requests for information under Legal's guidance.
Gather account history and draft responses for matters that need review.
- Help GRC process data subject requests and meet deadlines.
Follow approved identity-verification and data-handling procedures.
- Coordinate security questionnaires and data protection agreements, with Legal and GRC responsible for substantive review and approval.
- Track each case through completion, including after handoffs.
Record decisions, follow up on deadlines, and confirm the work is done before closing.
- Work with Support Engineering to test routing, AI bypass rules, auto-close protections, and alerts.
Investigate missed cases and verify fixes.
- Keep approved replies and handoff instructions current with Legal and GRC.
Arrange backup coverage so cases keep moving when you're out.
- Handle other sensitive support escalations.
Report backlog, response times, overdue cases, and recurring problems to Support, Legal, and GRC.
section_requirements:
- 5+ years in support, trust and safety, legal or privacy operations, or compliance, ideally at a technology company.
- Experience handling legal, privacy, or law enforcement requests.
- Working knowledge of GDPR, CCPA, and data subject requests.
- Judgment about when to involve Legal or GRC, and care with confidential and privileged information.
- Clear writing, including in sensitive customer conversations.
- Ability to manage competing deadlines and follow through without reminders.
- Experience improving support processes with technical teams, including automation and AI safeguards.
section_preferred:

- Paralegal, privacy, or compliance experience or certification.
- Experience with security questionnaires, SOC 2, ISO 27001, or HIPAA.
- Familiarity with AI products or data tools for case reviews.
